programme: No single recognizable module. The twelve factors span at least five unrelated developmental/signaling programmes: Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activation (CTNNB1), pancreatic/thyroid endocrine differentiation (GLIS3, NEUROG3, FOXA3), hepatic xenobiotic nuclear-receptor signaling (NR1I3, FOXA3), midbrain dopaminergic neuron specification (LMX1A), adrenal/gonadal steroidogenic and myogenic differentiation (TCF21), hematopoietic/myeloid lineage repression (GFI1), hypoxia-inducible transcription (EPAS1), and general-purpose chromatin/promoter factors (ETS2, ZNF143, ARID4B) with no known co-complex or shared pathway.
role_in_a: Only CTNNB1 has an independently documented role in Endometrioid_Cancer (Wnt pathway activation is a hallmark driver in endometrioid endometrial/ovarian carcinoma, consistent with its 0.97 Open Targets percentile and multiple case-report/review PMIDs). ZNF143 has weak ovarian-cancer literature (serous, not endometrioid). No other factor on the list has disease-specific placement.
role_in_b: GFI1, EPAS1, and GLIS3 each have isolated literature placing them in MS gene networks or autoimmune-risk colocalization, but through unrelated mechanisms (hematopoietic transcriptional repression, a hypoxia-linked lncRNA correlate, and cross-autoimmune GWAS colocalization respectively) — not a shared pathway with each other or with CTNNB1.
shared_axis: There is no mechanistic axis connecting these two diseases through this factor set: the developmental- and endocrine-lineage factors (LMX1A, NEUROG3, TCF21, FOXA3, NR1I3, GLIS3) have no documented role in either uterine epithelium or CNS demyelination, and the factors with some individual disease evidence (CTNNB1 in cancer; GFI1/EPAS1/GLIS3 in MS) act through different, non-overlapping pathways rather than a common module.
reasoning: Twelve factors recurring concordantly across patient groups is a statistical pattern, not evidence of a shared regulatory module; here the factors' known biology is too heterogeneous (pancreatic/thyroid endocrine TFs, a dopaminergic-neuron TF, a hepatic nuclear receptor, a steroidogenic TF, a hematopoietic repressor, a hypoxia TF, and generic chromatin factors) to name one process they run together. The one factor with strong disease-specific support, CTNNB1, is established only in endometrioid cancer and has no comparable documented role in MS in the material given, so it cannot carry a shared-axis story alone.
support: PMID 41903853, 41808247, 41510478, 41583123 — case reports/reviews placing CTNNB1/Wnt activation in endometrioid carcinoma, evidence for disease A only, not a shared axis; PMID 31482761 — GFI1 appears in an MS gene network, disease B only; PMID 31790618 — EPAS1-linked lncRNA correlates with MS severity, disease B only; PMID 26053495 — GLIS3 in cross-autoimmune-disease genetic colocalization including MS, disease B only; PMID 30885238 — ZNF143 expression in serous (not endometrioid) ovarian tumors, weak and off-target for disease A; PMID 41962616 — network analysis of toxin-induced MS pathology mentioning CTNNB1, too indirect to establish a Wnt-MS link.
how_to_falsify: Test whether CTNNB1, GFI1, EPAS1, and GLIS3 co-occupy a shared set of target promoters (ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN) or appear in the same co-expression module in either endometrioid tumor tissue or MS lesion/immune-cell single-cell data; if they cluster into one coordinately regulated gene program in either tissue, that would overturn the incoherent call. Absent that, the concordance across patient groups should be treated as a network-inference artifact rather than a biological finding.
caveats: 312 patient-group comparisons come from only 6 independent cohort pairs, so effective statistical independence is much lower than 312 suggests. Brain and uterine endometrium are anatomically and developmentally unrelated tissues, which raises the prior that any shared factor set is coincidental rather than mechanistic. The tissue-generic exclusion list already removed classic neural/differentiation master regulators shared by both tissues (TCF4, REST, NR3C1, SOX2, SOX9, SOX10, NKX2-1, ASCL1, NEUROD2, HOXD1, ID4, STAT4) — so what remains is depleted of the regulators most likely to explain a real cross-tissue link, and the residual list is enriched for idiosyncratic, lineage-restricted developmental TFs, consistent with an incoherent rather than a masked-coherent result.
